title: SRT values are wrong if you use time shift
description:
SRT values are incorrect when applying a time shift.

This is a follow up to Issue #18999.

The isue affects fields that calculate a time difference for service response
time (SRT) or similar deltas, as well as the GUI SRT tables.

The general problem is how the often used idiom relies on pinfo->abs_ts
not changing over time - but it does when a time shift is applied. With this
calls to nstime_delta() using pinfo->abs_ts does not give the desired result.

I have confirmed this issue in several dissectors and set up a frame work to
address it. Please see the first commit for the details. I have deliberately
(for now at least) included multiple commits to ease review:

- First commit setup up the frame work and fixes a few dissectors.
- Second commit fixes the simplest application of the common idiom.
- Further commits addresses more complicated uses.
- Regenerate ASN1 dissectors
- Update documentation.

The taps in ui/cli have not been updated (diameter and rpc) as time shift is
not possible with tshark.

Calls to e.g add_conversation_table_data() that reference pinfo->abs_ts have
been left as is. The table handles the delta well, and I feel it is desirable
to include the time shift in start times.

For the 50+ dissectors I have fixed, I have includes a summary including which
dissector fields have been confirmed fixed and status of SRT tables. In
almost all cases, I could confirm using a trace, which I referenced as well.

The following dissectors I suspect to be affected, but I could not confirm the
validity of attempts to fix them:

- bpv7:     Based on Issue #18479, dtn_tcpclv4_bpv7_transfer.pcapng, the
            bpv7.bundle.seen_time_diff field is affected, but I cannot tell if
            the fix influences bpv7.primary.lifetime_exp or how.
- btavdtp:  I am missing a trace to confirm.
- sbc:      No trace to confirm. Also interactis with btavdtp.
- ipmi:     No trace to confirm.
- signal-pdu: Works OK, but agg_data->sum_time_value_products might be wrong.

The following dissectors I do not understand well enough to fix without having
a reference trace that:

- ptp:      More complicated than I can confirm (Samples/ptpv2.pcap).
- sctp:     Need a trace exposing relevant fields.

The following dissectors do not seem affected in their use of nstime_delta():

- bthci_cmd:    Based on Bluetooth1.cap from Samples.
- bthci_evt:    Based on Bluetooth1.cap from Samples.
- esl:          Based on Issue #3677, ethercat_with_esl_trailing_header.pcap
- gsm_osmux:    Based on Issue #18337, osmux_call_bts_bsc_filtered.pcapng
- netflow:      Based on https://weberblog.net/the-ultimate-pcap/ (v20221220),
                tested with printf() for value comparison.
- tcpcl:        Based on (Issue #18479, dtn_tcpclv4_bpv7_transfer.pcapng
- transum:      Based on smbtorture.cap.gz
- umts_rlc:     Based on UMTS_FP_MAC_RLC_RRC_NBAP.pcap from Samples (filter on
                rlc.duplicate_of - not susceptible to time shift and ignored
                frames). The use of nstime_delta() is for duplicate detection
                that seems based on a single pass on each reload (ignore a
                packet). This turns out OK.

notes.body: Much easier to just trigger a redissection upon doing a time shift, I think.
The issue should be fixed in all the branches by redissecting, so I think you can close this.

Thanks for looking into this. I'm happy there was a much simpler fix.

I expect all is good, but if I find anything I'll bring it up separately.

commits_data.title: Time shift issue in the ieee802154 dissector
commits_data.message:
Time shift issue in the ieee802154 dissector

The dissectors stores a reftime and uses it for calculating a relative
ack time, both based on pinfo->abs_ts.

This is basically the time shift problem I am trying to address.

The one twist here, is that the delta time calculated with
nstime_delta() is only shown conditionally.

Dissector confirmed with a trace (+/- for tested/untested fields):

- ieee802154: -wpan.ack_time
  Have not found a trace to confirm

commits_data.title: Time shift issue in the iax2 dissector
commits_data.message:
Time shift issue in the iax2 dissector

The iax2 dissectors computes stores a start_time, computes an abstime
time stamp as well as a lateness relative to abstime.

The lateness is affected by a timeshift, which can be addressed by
taking shift into account.

When looking at the frame data, it feels a bit odd that the abstime does
not shift along when a time shift is applied. This patch does not
attempt to address this, though.

Dissector confirmed with a trace (+/- for tested/untested fields):

- iax2: +iax2.lateness
  https://wiki.wireshark.org/uploads/__moin_import__/attachments/SampleCaptures/h223-over-iax.pcap.gz

commits_data.title: Time shift issue in camel and tcap dissectors
commits_data.message:
Time shift issue in camel and tcap dissectors

Besides the usual idiom, there is logic to check if a request is new or
not which needs to be adapted akin to what was done for h225.

In comparisons, I have shifted the arguments a bit around to subtract a
guint from a time_t and compare the result to 0. I preferred this over
the existing cast.

One of the structures that track a begin_time member used in tcap are
also used by the ansi_tcap and camel dissectors - but neither use this
member.

Furthermore, only the tcap dissector contains the word begin_time.

With this, I feel it safe to update the tcap dissector.

While here, the related camel dissector was also updated.

NOTE 1: The tcap dissector has an end_time member that is updatedusing
abs_ts but is not referenced afterwards. If used later, it may be
susecptible to the time shift issue.

NOTE 2: These are ASN1 dissectors that needs to be regenerated.

Dissector confirmed with a trace (+/- for tested/untested fields):

- camel (ASN1): +camel.srt.deltatime22, +camel.srt.deltatime31, +SRT
  Issue #6781, camel.cap

- tcap (ASN1): +tcap.srt.sessiontime
  Issue #5637, C2G_RECIP9322955476.CAP

commits_data.title: Time shift issue in RPC dissectors
commits_data.message:
Time shift issue in RPC dissectors

packet-rpc.c uses the req_time member of rpc_call_info_value for SRT.

As rpc_call_info_value is passed around a lot, I took a different
approach and checked for code breaking if I temporarily removed req_time
as member.

1. In epan/dissectors/packet-rpc.h, rename req_time as req_time_xyz

2. Updated all references to req_time in packet-rpc.c.

3. Updated the reference to req_time in ui/cli/tap-rpcprogs.c.

4. Recompiling gave no errors, so no other code referenced this req_time.

As somewhat anticipated, all the RPC dissectors use the common code in
packet-rpc.c, so I reverted the changes and used the framework instead.

NOTE: I have not updated the ui/cli tap handler as tshark does not
allow for timeshift. It does feel appropriate to update it though.

Dissectors confirmed with a trace (+/- for tested/untested fields):

- rpc: +rpc.time, +SRT (portmap v3, mount v3, nfs v3)
  https://wiki.wireshark.org/uploads/__moin_import__/attachments/SampleCaptures/nfsv3.pcap.gz

commits_data.title: Time shift issue in usb dissectors
commits_data.message:
Time shift issue in usb dissectors

In packet-usb.c, SRT is handled using req_time in usb_trans_info_t.

1. Use a usb_trans_info_t variable to access one or more of these members:

    interface_info
    request_in
    setup
    u

    Seen in:

    epan/dissectors/packet-mbim.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-usb-com.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-usb-hid
    epan/dissectors/packet-usb-hid
    epan/dissectors/packet-usb-hid
    epan/dissectors/packet-usb-hub
    epan/dissectors/packet-usbms-bot.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-usbms-uasp.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-printer.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-video.c

2. Use as member usb_trans_info in usb_conv_info_t. Here
   usb_trans_info->req_time is only found in packet-usb.c.

3. Use as member trans_info in usb_tap_data_t. Here
trans_info->req_time is only found in packet-usb.c.

Dissectors confirmed with a trace (+/- for tested/untested fields):

- usb: +usb.time
  https://wiki.wireshark.org/uploads/__moin_import__/attachments/SampleCaptures/usb_memory_stick.pcap

commits_data.title: Time shift issue in scsi dissectors
commits_data.message:
Time shift issue in scsi dissectors

In packet-scsis.c, SRT is handled in two places:

1. Feeding to SRT tables as:

    add_srt_table_data(scsi_srt_table, ri->itlq->scsi_opcode, &ri->itlq->fc_time, pinfo);

2. Adding to the tree as scsi.time:

        nstime_delta(&delta_time, &pinfo->abs_ts, &itlq->fc_time);
        ti = proto_tree_add_time(scsi_tree, hf_scsi_time, tvb, 0, 0, &delta_time);

In both cases, "itlq->fc_time" refers dc_time as member of itlq_nexus_t.

Other dissectors are responsible for setting fc_time, which is done in:

packet-fc.c:
    While fc_time is used here, it is for local SRT using fc_exchange_t.

packet-fcp.c:
    Sets request_data->itlq->fc_time = pinfo->abs_ts.

packet-iscsi.c:
    Adds iscsi.time to the tree based on &cdata->itlq.fc_time.
    Sets cdata->itlq->fc_time = pinfo->abs_ts.

packet-ndmp.c:
    Sets ndmp_conv_data->task->itlq->fc_time = pinfo->abs_ts;

packet-rsvd.c:
    Sets rsvd_conv_data->task->itlq->fc_time = pinfo->abs_ts;

packet-scsi.c:
    Feeds SRT using add_srt_table_data()
    Adds scsi.time to the tree based on itlq->fc_time.

packet-usbms-bot.c:
    Sets itlq->fc_time = pinfo->abs_ts;

packet-usbms-uasp.c:
    Sets uitlq->itlq.fc_time = pinfo->abs_ts;

The above interactions are addressable

Dissectors confirmed with a trace (+/- for tested/untested fields):

- fcp: No trace, unfortunately.

- iscsi: +scsi.time, +iscsi.time, +SRT (SCSI/SSC)
  https://wiki.wireshark.org/uploads/__moin_import__/attachments/SampleCaptures/iscsi-tapel.gz

- ndmp: +scsi.time, +SRT (SCSI/SBC)
  Issue 3470, ndmp.cap from files.tar.gz
  NOTE: scsi.time is unhelpfully 0.0, but no longer affected by shift.

- rsvd: +scsi.time, +SRT (SCSI/SBC)
  Issue #10913, SQLServer-SMB2-selected.pcapng

- scsi: See other traces

- usbms-bot: +scsi.time, +SRT (SCSI/SBC) [usb.time still affected]
  USBMSC-USBPcap.pcapng from https://wiki.wireshark.org/uploads/36d216660e18783c8d2229ddc372f746/USBMSC-USBLL.7z

- usbms-uasp: No trace

commits_data.title: Time shift issue in dcerpc dissectors
commits_data.message:
Time shift issue in dcerpc dissectors

In general, SRT tracking for dcerpc related dissectors are done based on
dcerpc.time. However, I wanted to make sure that there is no other use
of the saved reftime in other dissectors.

packet-dcerpc.c uses dcerpc_call_value and the member req_time for SRT.
This struct is also used as the call_data member of dcerpc_info, usually
for a vraiable "di".

First, I have been tracking down the direct usage of dcerpc_call_value
outside of packet-dcerpc.c. This seems to fall into three categories:

1. Assigns di->call_data to a vriable to get to one of the members (pol,
   private_data or se_data), but does not use the variable itself in
   function calls. This is seen in:

    epan/dissectors/packet-dcerpc-lsa.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-dcerpc-netlogon.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-dcerpc-nt.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-dcerpc-samr.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-dcerpc-spoolss.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-dcerpc-svctl.c

2. Assigns a zeroed out static value to di->call_data, as seen in

    epan/dissectors/packet-kerberos.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-smb2.c
    epan/dissectors/packet-tnef.c

3. How plugins/epan/profinet/packet-dcerpc-pn-io.c sets up what it
   refers to as fake values for "di" and di->call_data.

As none of these dissectors use req_time directly, nor pass a
dcerpc_call_value variable in a function call, the use of req_time
outside of packet-dcerpc.c would have to be through the call_value
member of dcerpc_info. For this I searched for 'call_data->ptr',
which only appears in packet-dcerpc.c when calling add_srt_table_data().

I hence think it safe to use the new frame work in packet-dcerpc.c.

- dcerpc (winreg subdissector): +dcerpc.time, +SRT
  https://wiki.wireshark.org/uploads/__moin_import__/attachments/SampleCaptures/dcerpc-winreg-with-rpc-sec-verification-trailer.pcap

commits_data.title: Time shift issue in metamako dissector
commits_data.message:
Time shift issue in metamako dissector

metamako_time seems to be a saved timestamp, ideally close to the trace
capture time. The time difference is no longer correct with a time shift
and needs to take shift_offset into account.

The delta is hence not against a request value. Still, the time shift
issue applies.

The dissector sanity checks if the capture time of the frame is within
30 days of the time in the trailer. This check is done against
pinfo->abs_ts and is susceptible to time shift issues.

For the sanity check, I used a reference trace but modified the
timestamps of the first and the last frame:

- The first frame is now 30 days plus 30 minutes before the second.
- The last frame is 30 days plus 30 minutes after the second to last.

By default, the metamako trailer is not dissected. However, if you apply
a time shift of minus or plus one hour, the unpatched dissector will
dissect either the first or last frame.

To remedy this, I had to adapt the calculation for the sanity check.

NOTE: To test, I used HEURISTIC_ENABLE in proto_reg_handoff_metamako()
as I was not sure how to force the dissector to kick in otherwise. This
approach was a temporary reversal of merge request 522.

Dissector confirmed with a trace (+/- for tested/untested fields):

- metamako: +metamako.time.diff
  https://wiki.wireshark.org/uploads/__moin_import__/attachments/metamako_trailer.pcap/metamako_trailer.pcap
  metamako_trailer-sanity-checks.pcap (adapted as described above)

commits_data.title: Time shift issues with simple idiom updates
commits_data.message:
Time shift issues with simple idiom updates

These dissectors only needs updating for the simple idiom of saving a
reftime and adding values in the tree that can be handled with
proto_tree_add_srt() and proto_tree_add_srt_ret_val(), or in a few
cases using proto_srt_delta_since_ref_time() for adding a double.

The following conditions apply:

- The nstime_delta() call refers to pinfo->abs_ts.
- The reftime variable is only used for SRT purposes (including SRT
  table in Wireshark).
- the reftime variable is initiated using pinfo->abs_ts.
- The struct defining the reftime variable is only used by this
  dissector, even if defined in packet-xxx.h - or it is easy to verify
  that the reftime variable is not used by the other dissector (e.g.
  packet-cip.c uses enip_request_info_t from packet-enip.h, but not
  the req_time member).

When possible, I have checked against traces. I consider it correct
when a SRT packet detail value is unchanged after adding a time shift.
When a dissector has an SRT table in Wireshark, I have confirmed that
the values remain the same before and after a time shift.

When a trace is not available, I have only updated the code if it is a
very simple use of the idiom in the way that affect other dissectors.

NOTE on sbus: It calculates req_time on every visit, I think. At least
without the patch, the sbus.timeout and sbus.response_time values seem
to be reset when switching frames in the packet list. If shifting time,
the SRT value does change in the packet details of the current frame
(except the first response, at least) and column values are updated
irregularly. With the patch, sbus behaves well.

For ASN1 dissectors, I have regenerated packet-xxx.c for testing, but
not included the regenerated file in the patch at this point. If you
test, make sure to regenerate ASN1 dissectors.

commits_data.title: SRT values are wrong if you use time shift
commits_data.message:
SRT values are wrong if you use time shift

If using time shift, relative times relative to abs_ts will include the
time shift in the packet details. Similarly, Wireshark SRT tables will
include values with the time shift added.

When calculating delta times, or service response times, the common
idiom is to calculate the delta between pinfo->abs_ts and a stored
reference time. This calculation does not take any applied time shift
into account.

As an example, an ICMP response might show these values

    [Request frame: 1]
    [Response time: 492.204 ms]
    Timestamp from icmp data: May 31, 2013 00:45:17.283108000 CEST
    [Timestamp from icmp data (relative): 0.492283000 seconds]

If you apply a one hour shift, two values include that shift:

    [Request frame: 1]
    [Response time: 3600492.204 ms]
    Timestamp from icmp data: May 31, 2013 00:45:17.283108000 CEST
    [Timestamp from icmp data (relative): 3600.492283000 seconds]

While this could be addressed by adding an nstime_delta() call applying
pinfo->fd->shift_offset in most places calling nstime_delta(), I have
tried to tackle this in a way that codifies when SRT related values are
saved or calculated.

This patch sets up a frame work for addressing this in several
dissectors using the following functions:

- proto_tree_add_srt(tree, hfindex, pinfo, reftime)

  Add an item to tree with the relative time between reftime and the
  time info in pinfo. The item is always added as a generated item for
  consistency (most dissectors do this, a few don't).

- proto_tree_add_srt_ret_val(tree, hfindex, pinfo, reftime, *delta)

  Same, but update delta with the computed value for the caller to use.

- proto_srt_set_ref_time(reftime, pinfo)

  Set reftime based on time info in pinfo. Used in call/response
  handlers that currently use reftime = pinfo->abs_ts. This is needed
  when revisiting all frames with a time shift in place (apply a shift,
  then mark a packet as ignored).

- proto_srt_delta_since_ref_time(delta, pinfo, reftime)

  Compute the delta between time info in pinfo and reftime.

This approach simplifies code in most affected dissectors.

For SRT tables, add_srt_table_data() has been updated as well.

This commit includes updates to a few dissectors to highlight some of
the considerations needed for other dissectors.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

packet-smb2.c uses the common idiom, applicable to most dissectors:

1. On first visit, save a reference time when tracking requests:

        ssi                  = wmem_new0(wmem_file_scope(), smb2_saved_info_t);
        ssi->msg_id          = ssi_key.msg_id;
        ssi->frame_req       = pinfo->num;
        ssi->req_time        = pinfo->abs_ts;
        ssi->extra_info_type = SMB2_EI_NONE;
        g_hash_table_insert(si->conv->unmatched, ssi, ssi);

When updating the code, ssi->req_time will be set like this instead:

        proto_srt_set_ref_time(&ssi->req_time, pinfo);

2. When adding the delta time to the tree, the common idiom is:

        if (ssi->frame_req) {
                proto_item *tmp_item;
                nstime_t    t, deltat;

                tmp_item = proto_tree_add_uint(header_tree, hf_smb2_response_to, tvb, 0, 0, ssi->frame_req);
                proto_item_set_generated(tmp_item);
                t = pinfo->abs_ts;
                nstime_delta(&deltat, &t, &ssi->req_time);
                tmp_item = proto_tree_add_time(header_tree, hf_smb2_time, tvb,
                0, 0, &deltat);
                proto_item_set_generated(tmp_item);
        }

The updated code is:

        if (ssi->frame_req) {
                proto_item *tmp_item;

                tmp_item = proto_tree_add_uint(header_tree, hf_smb2_response_to, tvb, 0, 0, ssi->frame_req);
                proto_item_set_generated(tmp_item);
                proto_tree_add_srt(header_tree, hf_smb2_time, pinfo, &ssi->req_time);
        }

As proto_tree_add_srt() calculates delta and marks items as generated:

- The nstime_delta() call is not needed.
- The nstime_t variables can be removed.
- The last call to proto_item_set_generated() can be removed.
- In some dissectors, a proto_item variable can be removed, too.

3. The SRT table is updated with add_srt_table_data().

No code change is needed as the reference time is set with time shift
included and add_srt_table_data() now handles the time shift.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

packet-icmp.c and packet-icmpv6.c both use icmp_transaction_t for SRT,
specifually the rqst_time member.

Rather than tracking down individual uses, I prefer to address both
dissectors together. Some dissectors may both use the struct, while only
one accesses the member.

As seen in other dissectors, too, icmp shows the delta as a double:

        nstime_delta(&ns, &pinfo->abs_ts, &icmp_trans->rqst_time);
        icmp_trans->resp_time = ns;
        resp_time = nstime_to_msec(&ns);
        it = proto_tree_add_double_format_value(tree, hf_icmp_resptime,
                                                NULL, 0, 0, resp_time,
                                                "%.3f ms", resp_time);
        proto_item_set_generated(it);

Here, and for a similar call in icmpv6, the call to nstime_delta() must be
replaced with this:

        proto_srt_delta_since_ref_time(&ns, pinfo, &icmp_trans->rqst_time);

Both dissectors also assign ns to the resp_time member of
icmp_transaction_t for tapping. The output of tshark -z icmp,srt and
icmpv6,srt is identical with and without the fix.

NOTE 1: two relative timestamps are calculated for ICMP:

1. The double above, which as a response time should stay the same when
   a time shift is in effect.

2. A "Timestamp from icmp data", now added with proto_tree_add_srt() is
   more complicated.

   Given that the icmp data has a fixed value based on trace data, one
   could argue that with a time shift in place that the shown value
   should include the shift.

   However, I think practically the icmp.data_time_relative value would
   be used as a delta between when the timestamp was set in frame data
   and when the data was captured (e.g. in the echo request). In that
   use case, the time shift should be omitted - which I opted for.

NOTE 2: The icmp dissector has other uses of pinfo->abs_ts that should be
investigated separately, possibly including the math around setting
icmp.data_time_relative discussed above.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

packet-dns.c also generally uses the same idiom, but before updating the
reference times check if this is a retransmission:

        /* Has not enough time elapsed that we consider this request a retransmission? */
        nstime_delta(&request_delta, &pinfo->abs_ts, &dns_trans->req_time);
        if (nstime_to_sec(&request_delta) < (double)retransmission_timer) {
          retransmission = TRUE;
        } else {

This case is different from packet-icmp.c in that the computation only
is performed on first visit of a frame. This calculation will then be
good as long as you only apply time shifts. If you ignore a packet,
however, frames are revisited with a time shift in place.

Again, the nstime_delta() must be replaced:

        proto_srt_delta_since_ref_time(&request_delta, pinfo, &dns_trans->req_time);

------------------------------------------------------------------------

packet-h225.c again uses the same idiom, but also has an if statement
that involves direct computations based on pinfo->abs_ts.secs.

I unrolled the if statement and use proto_srt_delta_since_ref_time().
This required adding a "duplicate" variable.

The SRT table is not updated using add_srt_table_data() and an unpacthed
wireshark shows correct values.

The patch is tested against h225-ras.pcap from issue #6955 and a custom
h225-ras-dup.pcap trace used to check the duplicate detection by:

1. Extract the last two UDP frames from h225-ras.pcap to x.pcap
2. By hand, change the time stamps by one hour in x.pcap
3. Copy x.pcap as y.pcap and shift time stamps by another minute
4. Merge h225-ras.pcap, x.pcap and y.pcap into h225-ras-dup.pcap

In the merged trace, the last two frames should match h225.ras.dup.
Without the fix, there are no duplicates with a time shift of one hour.
With the fix, the packet details and duplicates are correct.

NOTE: This is an ASN1 dissector, so packet-h225.c must be regenerated.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
